review.summary: The commit changes JET's `@test`/`@test_*` expression rewriting in the virtual top-level process so that test expressions containing anonymous functions defined under conditional (`&&`, `||`, `if`, `comparison`) positions are outlined into a zero-argument thunk before value-discarding transformation. Per the inline rationale, the prior behavior forced concrete execution of the branch condition because virtual processing concretizes top-level closure definitions; the fix keeps such closures inside a method body so inference analyzes the control flow instead of concretely evaluating the condition. That is a correctness fix to analysis behavior on already-supported input, not a new user-facing capability.
review.evidence: Production change is confined to one file (src/toplevel/virtualprocess.jl) touching `replace_test` and `replace_test_macrocall`, with new internal-only predicates (`is_test_expression_thunk_safe`, `has_conditionally_defined_test_function`, `should_wrap_test_expression_in_thunk`, `wrap_test_expression_in_thunk`). A matching test file is modified (test/toplevel/test_virtualprocess.jl). Runtime evidence reports strict_differential = stable_differential over 3 repetitions with the fixed full suite passing, trigger_mode = test_patch_suite, indicating reproducible fail-before/pass-after behavior. Minimization kept 3 of 5 hunks and reports globally_minimal with all kept hunks necessary, consistent with a single coherent fix rather than bundled unrelated edits.

review.validation_risks: The fix is heuristic and driven by allow-lists of expression heads; a validating test may assert on internals of the rewritten expression or on JET report counts, which are sensitive to Julia version and Test stdlib macro expansion, raising version-coupling risk. Because the guard depends on syntactic shape, a minimized trigger test could pass for reasons unrelated to the concretization bug. Behavior also depends on `Base.remove_linenums!` and gensym-based thunks, so any test comparing expressions structurally could be brittle.
review.suggested_tests: Add focused tests that (1) run virtual top-level processing on `@test cond && (x -> f(x))(1)` and `@test if cond; y -> g(y); else; z -> h(z); end`, asserting the branch condition is not concretely executed (e.g., a side-effecting condition that would mutate a flag or throw if run) while inference still analyzes both branches; (2) cover `@test skip=<expr>` with a conditionally defined closure to exercise the `conditionally_evaluated = true` path; (3) cover `@test_throws`/`@test_broken` variants through `replace_test_macrocall`; (4) negative cases that must stay inline, such as expressions containing assignments, `local`/`global`, named function definitions, `return`/`break`, and unrecognized macro calls, verifying no thunk wrapping occurs; (5) `do`-block form `@test f(x) do a; ...; end` under a conditional. Run each repeatedly to confirm determinism.
